title: The Pratfall Effect

scenes.text: Making a mistake can make people like you *more*
scenes.vo: Here's something weird. Making a small mistake can make people like you more.

scenes.text: People listened to a quiz contestant who knew *every answer*
scenes.vo: In an old experiment, people listened to a recording of a quiz contestant who got almost every answer right.

scenes.text: Then he *spilled coffee* all over himself
scenes.vo: In one version, at the end, he clumsily spilled coffee all over himself.
People liked the clumsy version more. He felt more human, more like one of us.

scenes.text: But only if he was already *good*
scenes.vo: But here's the catch. When the contestant wasn't very smart, spilling the coffee made people like him less.
This is called the pratfall effect. A pratfall is just a silly fall or blunder.

scenes.text: Good at something? Laughing at your small mistakes makes you *relatable*.
scenes.vo: So if you're good at something, don't hide your small mistakes. Laughing at them makes you relatable.

caption:
Being perfect is a bit scary. A small slip-up makes people like you more. ☕ That's the pratfall effect.

Do you like people more when they admit mistakes? 👇
source: Aronson, E., Willerman, B. & Floyd, J. (1966). The effect of a pratfall on increasing interpersonal attractiveness. Psychonomic Science, 4(6).
